Coherent Corp. Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results

November 04, 2026 16:05 ET  | Source: Coherent Corp. Coherent Corp.

  • Q1 REVENUE OF $2.37B, INCREASED 50% Y/Y AND 56% Y/Y ON A PRO FORMA BASIS
  • Q1 GAAP GROSS MARGIN OF 39.1%, INCREASED 254 bps Y/Y; Q1 NON-GAAP GROSS MARGIN OF 40.6%, INCREASED 184 bps Y/Y
  • Q1 GAAP EPS OF $1.90, INCREASED $0.71 Y/Y; Q1 NON-GAAP EPS OF $2.09, INCREASED $0.93 Y/Y

SAXONBURG, Pa., Nov. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Coherent Corp. (NYSE: COHR) (“Coherent,” “We,” or the “Company”), a global leader in photonics, announced financial results today for its first quarter of fiscal year 2027 ended September 30, 2026.

Revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 was $2.37 billion, with GAAP gross margin of 39.1% and GAAP net income of $1.90 per diluted share. On a non-GAAP basis, gross margin was 40.6% with net income per diluted share of $2.09.

“Q1 marked a strong start to fiscal 2027, with pro forma revenue up 56% year over year and non-GAAP EPS up 80%,” said Jim Anderson, CEO. “Our established businesses delivered strong growth, while new growth areas are beginning to ramp. As AI datacenters transition from copper to optical connectivity, Coherent’s broad photonics platform and manufacturing scale position us to help customers meet rising needs for bandwidth and energy efficiency. We expect fiscal 2027 pro forma revenue growth to exceed 60%.”

Sherri Luther, CFO, said, “Our Q1 results delivered substantial operating leverage and durable gross margin expansion, driven by pricing optimization and cost improvements. This margin strength gives us the confidence to raise our longer-term target. We expect to achieve our first quarter with non-GAAP gross margin above 45% before the end of calendar 2028.”

Business Outlook – Second Quarter Fiscal 2027(1)

  • Revenue for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 is expected to be between $2.55 billion and $2.75 billion.
  • Gross margin percentage for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 is expected to be between 40% and 42% on a non-GAAP basis.
  • Total operating expenses for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 are expected to be between $430 million and $450 million on a non-GAAP basis.
  • Tax rate for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 is expected to be between 18% and 20% on a non-GAAP basis.
  • EPS for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 is expected to be between $2.28 and $2.48 on a non-GAAP basis.

Additional Revenue and Gross Margin Guidance

  • Expect to achieve our first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of fiscal 2027.
  • Expect fiscal 2027 pro forma revenue growth to exceed 60%, more than double our fiscal 2026 pro forma growth rate.
  • Expect first $4 billion revenue quarter in fiscal 2028.
  • New Gross Margin Target: Expect to achieve our first quarter with non-GAAP gross margin above 45% before the end of calendar 2028.

(1) The Company has not provided a quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking non-GAAP gross margin percentage, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP tax rate and non-GAAP earnings per share, because we cannot, without unreasonable efforts, forecast certain items required to develop comparable GAAP measures. These items include, without limitation, restructuring charges, integration, site consolidation and other expenses, foreign exchange gains (losses), and share based compensation expense.  The variability of these items could significantly impact our future GAAP financial results and we believe that the inclusion of any such reconciliations would imply a degree or precision that could be confusing or misleading to investors.

About Coherent

Coherent is the global photonics leader. We harness photons to drive innovation. Industry leaders in the datacenter, communications, and industrial markets rely on Coherent’s world-leading technology to fuel their own innovation and growth.

Founded in 1971 and operating in more than 20 countries, Coherent brings the industry’s broadest, deepest technology stack; unmatched supply chain resilience; and global scale to help its customers solve their toughest technology challenges. For more information, please visit us at coherent.com.

(1)Integration, site consolidation and other costs include retention and severance payments and other integration costs related to the acquisition of Coherent, Inc., implementation of common technology systems and costs related to business divestitures.
(2)Financing fees include debt extinguishment costs and various fees related to closing the new Credit Agreement and repricing our Term Loan B.
(3)Restructuring charges include non-cash impairment charges for production assets and improvements on leased facilities, severance, contract termination costs and other costs related to the restructuring plans.
(4)Impairment of assets held-for-sale relate to several entities classified as held-for-sale.
(5)Gain on sale of business is due to the sale of our aerospace and defense business.
(6)Gain on sale of investment is due to the sale of shares in an equity method investment.
(7)The Company adopted a full-year, normalized tax rate for the computation of the non-GAAP income tax provision beginning in fiscal year 2026. We believe this approach provides investors with a more consistent view of our underlying operating performance. In estimating the full-year non-GAAP normalized tax rate, the Company utilized a full-year financial projection that considers multiple factors such as changes to the Company's current operating structure, expected reserve changes for the year, and other significant tax matters to the extent they are applicable to the full fiscal year financial projection. In addition to the adjustments described above, this normalized tax rate excludes the impact of share-based awards, amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, integration and restructuring charges, foreign exchange gain/(loss), and certain tax valuation allowances.
   
  For fiscal years 2026 and 2027, the Company's non-GAAP normalized tax rate is 19%. This projected normalized tax rate was applied to each quarter of fiscal year 2026 and 2027. The Company's non-GAAP normalized tax rate on non-GAAP net income may be adjusted during the year to account for events or trends that the Company believes materially impact the original annual non-GAAP normalized tax rate including, but not limited to, significant changes resulting from tax legislation, acquisitions or dispositions, entity structures or operational changes and other significant events. These additional non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered substitutes for any measures derived in accordance with GAAP and may be inconsistent with similar measures presented by other companies.
